records.c: One BASIC line in the unpacked image. Its SYS expression is (2063), the first machine-code instruction at $080F.
Stops interrupts, installs a fresh stack and clears decimal mode. Sets up the C64, draws the life-strip scaffolding and enables interrupts before entering the title selection.
Resets state for a new game, sets up the first player and enters the round loop.
Stops sound, resets working state, copies and draws the selected round and initializes its HUD and actors.
Scans the keyboard and joystick, offers the editor, updates actors and resolves contact with the room grid, then handles the timer, bonus state and pacing.
Adds the round increment to the logical round index, updates the player record, delays and wraps index $22 to zero.
Waits with the death state displayed and subtracts a life. Goes back to round setup if the signed result stays nonnegative.
Embedded developer address and telephone text. It lies between the end of the game-control block and the display-enable routine.
Sets the VIC display-enable bit without disturbing the other control bits.
Clears the VIC display-enable bit and the high raster compare bit before a bulk redraw.
Packs six displayed score digits into the three-byte best score at $52–$54.
Fills 22 bitmap cells at a vertical stride of $0140, beginning at $6278, with $55 or $AA stripes and sets the corresponding screen bytes starting at $404F to $FC.
Draws both strips of static text and calls the score, time, bonus, stocks and room-number drawing routines.
Selects the title layout, blits its backdrop and overlay, renders the credit text at two bitmap positions and waits for input or a delay.
Bitmap glyphs for the Tecmo copyright line, padded for its title layout and terminated by zero.
Bitmap glyphs for the Probe Software copyright line and its zero terminator.
Displays the title and draws the player-count choice. Input bit 5 toggles the choice and bit 4 confirms it.
Split address bytes for the one-player and two-player prompts drawn by $0A59.
High pointer bytes for the paired player-count prompt addresses.
Two zero-terminated lines for the menu, selected by the current player-count bit.
Glyph string for PLAYERS - TWO. The preceding zero-terminated line is the one-player alternative.
Draws the object-value guide. If no input was found it also draws the high-score page, then restarts the title sequence.
Compares the current three-byte score with the stored best. A higher score replaces the best and sets the flag for rendering a new entry.
Converts the saved best to six glyphs and edits the two printed room digits in the score line if the new-best flag is set.
Converts the high and low BCD nibbles of A to glyphs, appending them to the score line at $0D3C + X.
Makes a digit glyph, using a space for zero before the first significant digit. Y tracks whether a significant digit has been emitted.
Selects the scoreboard layout, draws the heading then blits ten 39-byte text rows over the backdrop.
Forty glyphs centered around the scoreboard heading, plus its zero terminator.
Ten fixed-stride rows of glyph codes, with rank, six score positions, player name and room. Each 39-byte record ends in zero.
Score field and sortable text in leaderboard row 1. The stored score reads 100000. The rank prefix lies before this field.
Score field and sortable text in leaderboard row 2. The stored score reads 50000. The rank prefix lies before this field.
Score field and sortable text in leaderboard row 3. The stored score reads 20000. The rank prefix lies before this field.
Score field and sortable text in leaderboard row 4. The stored score reads 10000. The rank prefix lies before this field.
Score field and sortable text in leaderboard row 5. The stored score reads 5000. The rank prefix lies before this field.
Score field and sortable text in leaderboard row 6. The stored score reads 2000. The rank prefix lies before this field.
Score field and sortable text in leaderboard row 7. The stored score reads 1000. The rank prefix lies before this field.
Score field and sortable text in leaderboard row 8. The stored score reads 500. The rank prefix lies before this field.
Score field and sortable text in leaderboard row 9. The stored score reads 200. The rank prefix lies before this field.
The tenth displayed row doubles as the editable line. Score conversion writes the beginning, and the round digits are patched separately.
Second digit in the last score row; the score reader pairs it with the previous glyph.
Byte immediately preceding the name, used with X as a biased address to erase the previous letter.
Ten score-entry character cells. The last-row name is displayed on the score table and read by the editor-enable comparison.
First room digit in the final score row, filled from the high nibble at $1B1F.
Second room digit in the final score row, filled from the low nibble.
Tests ten name glyphs in the final score row against the stored checksum. It sets the editor-enable byte at $5A when the adjusted bytes all match.
Ten expected bytes for $0D5C. The comparison adds $32 and the character index to the stored player-name glyph.
Draws the score-screen background and eleven rows of object-value legends, then blits the occupied foreground cells that illustrate those legends.
Eleven 39-byte rows of panel text pairing score awards with fire, scroll, time, life and fairy descriptions.
Uses A as a bounded delay count. Polls the game controls between passes and exits early when the mapped controls are nonzero.
Starts tune 3, then checks the new-best flag. A qualifying score opens the name-entry screen, clears ten glyphs and reads selections until the end glyph is chosen.
Draws the cursor marker below the glyph position selected by the name length. At ten letters it returns without a marker.
Glyph $66 and terminator for the cursor under the high-score name field.
Updates the input and compares it with the previous sample. Repeated input reduces the delay toward $10.
Draws the writable final score row, with the name being entered, on the score-entry screen.
Displays 25 glyphs from the cyclic 39-entry alphabet starting at the current selection offset.
Cyclic 39-glyph chooser for score names, including the delete and finish glyphs at $69 and $6A.
One-glyph mutable string for the letter-wheel blitter. The glyph is patched before each draw.
Appends a glyph while the name length is below ten. The delete glyph replaces the prior position with a dot and decrements the length if it is nonzero.
Repeatedly compares neighboring leaderboard scores from right to left and swaps the first 32 bytes of each pair when out of order, stopping after a pass with no swaps.
Addresses of sortable portions of successive leaderboard rows. The sort uses adjacent pairs and preserves the fixed rank field.
High half of the first score-row pointer. This operand is indexed by double the row number.
Low half of the following score-row pointer, relative to the first.
Overlapping high-byte alias used when the sort advances to the next score row.
When two-player mode is selected, makes the initial zero-page copy at $06B6 and sets the active player field to one.
In two-player mode, swaps the active zero page and the alternate player's image at $06B6 if its status byte is zero.
Copies the remaining-time bytes to the writable award slot, shifts the 24-bit value right four bits and adds it using the score routine.
Starts the selected tune while preserving the caller's X and Y through two saved bytes.
Starts the selected sound effect while preserving the actor or tile indices held in X and Y.
Compares the three-byte time counter with the indexed threshold. When it crosses the threshold, updates $4E and switches between tunes zero and one.
Fills eleven screen color bytes at $4011–$401B with A.
High pair of decimal digits for each room’s time-bonus comparison.
Middle BCD byte in the comparison with the live time; the least significant comparison byte is zero.
Clears the sixteen active flags and sets the player frame from the facing field.
Draws the backdrop, prints GAME OVER and delays before returning.
GAME OVER glyph codes and zero terminator for the bitmap string helper.
Draws the bare backdrop and announces the round, then shows its exit and key. For a flagged preview, animates the exit through three tile shapes before starting the room.
Clears the two low base-100 digits and takes the high digit from the round table at $1B43, with the message flag masked off.
Calls the time-expiry effect at zero. With the player in state $04 it leaves the timer alone, otherwise it subtracts two in decimal mode.
Fills the sixteen actor sprite pointers at $04F0 with $7F, the blank sprite frame.
Runs the 32-count X loop on each increment of A. Counts Y complete A wraps before returning.
Stops CIA1 timer A, selects the VIC bank at $4000 and sets CIA1 directions for scanning. Installs the IRQ and NMI entries in the hardware vectors in RAM.
Immediately returns from an NMI without changing the interrupted code’s registers.
Copies 47 initial bytes at $1395 to VIC-II offsets $2E down through $00.
Initial register bytes for $D000–$D02E, including bitmap and multicolor settings, raster timing, pointer bases and colors.
Looks up the room slot via $208C, then passes the slot to the grid and backdrop loader.
Maps the logical round through $208C before loading its actor record.
Busy-waits for the counter at $2F to reach two, then clears the counter. The fourth raster pass increments it.
Selects reset-mask bit 0 so $13EE restores the corresponding zero-page defaults.
Selects reset-mask bit 1 on the shared zero-page initializer.
Selects reset-mask bit 2 before rebuilding round state.
Walks the reset-mask table in reverse and copies each matching initial value to the associated zero-page address.
Default values indexed by destination zero-page byte during the selected reset passes.
Per-byte masks that select which reset pass restores the paired zero-page value.
Takes the room slot in A. Copies a 143-byte foreground grid and the selected 143-byte backdrop to $0510 and $059F, then derives the backdrop palette selectors.
Maps each of the 36 physical room slots to a backdrop record at $B6CC.
Six shared color RAM values, one per selected backdrop.
Six VIC background-color values, applied after drawing the backdrop.
Copies the slot’s 128 initial actor bytes from $EA00 + A × 128 to $0400. Clears the upper actor work lanes, blanks all sprite pointers and re-enables construction of the raster sprite lists.
Saves A, Y and X, then selects one of four IRQ branches through the split address table indexed by $12.
Advances the IRQ phase modulo four, acknowledges the VIC raster source and restores X, Y and A before returning.
Low bytes for four interrupt phases, followed by their high bytes. Each target publishes one sprite band.
Four IRQ target high bytes paired with the lows at $1590.
Publishes the list at offset $00 and schedules the next raster interrupt for line 94.
Publishes the list at offset $22 and schedules line 148.
Publishes the list at offset $44 and schedules line 202.
Publishes the list at offset $66, prepares the next sprite lists, ticks audio and updates the fireball-stock animation. Advances the main-loop clock and schedules line 40.
When the main loop enables list construction, clears the four masks and fills the pointer lanes with a blank frame. Offers each live actor to the band assignment routine.
Chooses a band or adjacent pair of bands from the actor’s vertical coordinate.
Sets the enable and optional high-X bits and writes the coordinates, shape and color to the first 34-byte sprite band buffer.
Saves one actor in the second band, using the slot bit at $E99C for its enable and X overflow masks.
Copies the selected actor's frame, color and position to the third band and sets the band-specific masks.
Fills the fourth band fields for one slot. The following helpers choose a free position in one or two consecutive bands.
Scans a mask from bit 7 down. Y is the highest available position or negative if none remains.
Shifts the occupied mask right to find the lowest clear bit. Returns Y=8 when all eight slots are occupied.
Copies one 34-byte buffer into sprite enable and high-X masks, sprite positions, the pointer table at $43F8 and sprite colors. Input X is the buffer offset.
Passes the top panel template at $17F0 to the solid-text blitter for the bitmap row at $6000.
Forty bitmap glyph codes for the top panel labels and spaces reserved for numbers, followed by zero.
Passes the bottom panel template at $182C to the text blitter at bitmap address $7CC0.
Two rows of forty glyphs for the life, round and fairy panel and the surrounding blank cells, followed by zero.
Reads a zero-terminated string from ($04). Draws each glyph through the overlay helper and sets the corresponding screen cell to $11. Preserves X and Y.
Finds eight bytes at $FC00 + code × 8. Converts them through $2800 and uses the $CF00 mask table to merge them over the bitmap. Advances the destination one cell.
Draws a zero-terminated string at ($02), from ($04). Writes a black screen-byte palette and color 1, one cell per glyph. Preserves X and Y.
Copies the eight bytes at $FC00 + A × 8 to the bitmap pointer in $02/$03 and advances that pointer eight bytes. Restores Y.
Copies one glyph into the current bitmap cell and steps the destination pointer. This is the body of the entry at $1931.
Gives up precedence over down, left precedence over right, and block casting precedence over the secondary action when both are held.
Inverts the five joystick lines on CIA1 port A and adds the mapped keyboard bits. $2D suppresses held action bits across successive samples while allowing direction holds.
Tests eight selected row/column pairs against the buffered keyboard matrix and merges their logical control bits into $13.
Matrix row-buffer offsets indexed by the eight logical keyboard control slots.
Masks selecting one column from each keyboard row for the movement and action controls.
Bit flags ORed into the joystick latch when the corresponding sampled key is held.
Drives each row selector into CIA1 port A. Accepts two successive equal reads of port B, then inverts and saves the column mask in zero page.
Single-zero row-drive patterns for scanning CIA1 port B. The reverse loop selects row 0 first.
Writes $CC to the bitmap’s screen-byte and color RAM planes across all 1,000 cells.
Adds 13 times Y to X using the row-base table at $E1F4.
For cell X, looks up the bitmap and screen-byte addresses and derives the corresponding color RAM pointer.
Looks up the foreground and backdrop codes at X, optionally translating the foreground through $2600, then builds their bitmap pointers and the foreground palette pointer.
Entry after the foreground fetch. A supplies the tile code while X still selects the backdrop and destination index.
Blits the 143 backdrop tiles, then writes the selected shared background color to $D021.
Copies one 24-byte upper half and one 24-byte lower half to two multicolor bitmap rows, with accompanying color RAM writes.
Prints the bonus-prison message when bit 7 of the room table is set, and inserts the two round digits from $1B1F before drawing the round string.
Glyphs for BONUS PRISON with zero terminator, drawn on rounds whose timer-table entry sets bit 7.
Bitmap text template for the room announcement. Two digit cells are patched from the room table before the blit.
First of the two room digits patched by the announcement routine.
Second room digit, after the literal hyphen and before the terminator.
Packed decimal round pairs with the first digit in the high nibble. The final two logical slots contain zero.
Per-round high byte of the time bonus. Bit 7 requests the BONUS PRISON announcement and is masked out before the time starts.
Renders every cell of the room, whether empty or occupied, using the foreground and backdrop blitter.
Visits the same 143 cells but skips foreground code zero before drawing.
Sets up one tile’s source pointers, then resolves its destination and composites it over the backdrop using the per-byte mask table.
Takes foreground and backdrop source pointers and blits their two rows into the bitmap. The mask table keeps background pixels where the overlay pixels are zero.
Samples the upper pair of tile collision points relative to actor X.
Tests tile collision bits at horizontal offsets 1 and 8 along Y offset 16.
Tests the tile at X offset -1 against the north and south ends of the side.
Tests the tiles at X offset 10 and Y offsets 2 and 15.
Tests the adjacent X offsets 4 and 5, one unit below the actor origin.
Reads the tile reached by the supplied offset and stores the first raw cell code and its index for the combined two-probe collision check.
Adds the selected actor's Y and X to the two offsets passed in Y and A, then converts the resulting world position to a tile.
Looks up the tile reached by adding A and Y to actor X’s coordinates, saves its cell index and returns bit 0 of its collision class.
Converts world coordinates A,Y to a cell in the 13 × 11 room. Outside the room returns tile $01 and index $FF.
Uses A as the new foreground code and X as the cell index, writes the room buffer and redraws that cell.
Samples the tile below the player’s origin at offset (4,8), then jumps via the split table for raw tile codes below $40.
Low operand byte patched from the tile dispatch table.
High operand byte in the tile handler jump, patched for the same cell.
Split address table for 64 raw tile codes. $1CB0 uses these bytes to patch the dispatch jump.
High half of the raw tile dispatch table, paired with lows at $1CCF.
Empty default tile handler. Returns without touching the room or player.
Signals a completed room and clears the temporary exit-animation flag.
Doubles BCD time, then adds the standard pickup award and removes the cell.
Multiplies BCD time by five, adds the pickup's score and clears its cell.
Doubles time if the threshold flag is set after awarding the pickup points.
Applies the alternate threshold test to determine whether to double time.
Takes an inactive actor slot, places a type $0B fairy at the exit with shape $47 and awards points. If all slots are occupied, returns before touching the exit.
Byte offsets of score awards for foreground objects, used by $1DCC to select a three-byte award at $1F57.
Selects a BCD award from the tile-derived offset, plays the pickup sound and clears the sampled room tile.
Raises the life counter up to five and redraws lives before processing the pickup score and clearing its cell.
Scans existing stock for code $08 and changes the first match to fireball code 0. Redraws stock and applies the pickup score.
Upgrades the first $08 fireball-stock slot to code $04 before applying the common pickup award.
Replaces the first stock entry of type zero with type four if one exists, then redraws stock, awards points and removes the pickup.
Increases the number of fireball positions up to eight, redraws the icons and processes the pickup award.
Marks active actors of type $03 or $04 for their secondary handler by writing one to their phase slot. Then gives the standard pickup award.
Removes the key cell, sets the exit flag, animates the exit through tiles $06 and $07 and leaves tile $08 in the foreground buffer.
Sets the round increment to two before entering the exit-opening animation.
Uses the stored sampled cell index, clears its foreground byte and draws the resulting cell.
Counts Y wraps of the accumulator through increments without the longer inner delay loop.
Scans foreground codes for an exit in the range $04–$08 and returns the matching index in X, or $8F if the scan runs out.
Scans the foreground for one of the four key codes $03, $11, $2B or $31.
Adds a three-byte packed-decimal score award beginning at table index X. Saves a copy of the award and redraws the relevant score fields.
Packed-decimal award bytes read in three-byte groups by $1F39.
Advances Y by one overall and returns (Y + 1) modulo four in A. The BCD award loop uses zero to end its three-byte add.
Writable three-byte award slot initialized by the high-score time-bonus path.
Middle byte of the calculated time award.
Most significant byte before and after the time-bonus shift.
Draws the active-player digit in the top strip by converting $2B to its glyph.
Draws the current life stock using the HUD bitmap and palette instead of a hardware sprite.
Chooses the bitmap start by the current stock and draws the common stock graphic followed by one glyph for each stored fireball type.
Operand and return at the end of the stock drawing loop.
Return after drawing the selected stored fireballs.
Eight bitmap addresses in descending steps of sixteen. The blitter indexes with twice the stock, with a two-byte bias.
On each fourth call changes the display palette by $11 and writes two neighboring cells in each of two display rows per fireball-stock counter.
Draws two glyphs for the logical round using the byte tables at $2044 and $2068.
First displayed glyph for each logical round marker.
Second displayed glyph for each logical round marker.
Room data order for the foreground and actor initialization loaders, including the inserted rooms.
Converts the fairy counter to a digit and draws it in the lower strip.
Points the bitmap cursor into the top HUD and passes the player's three score bytes to the common BCD printer.
Prints the three-byte time counter into the top HUD, with a zero glyph for an empty counter.
Clears the bonus area and prints the three-byte points-award value with the common BCD routine.
Splits a packed BCD byte into two glyphs, skipping leading spaces until a nonzero digit has been emitted.
Adds the digit base $30 except for leading zero, where it returns a space. Y remembers whether a nonzero digit has been printed.
Uses Y to select glyphs for the multi-cell HUD icon and copies its rows to the bitmap.
Table of HUD glyphs indexed by the requested large-icon offset. This base supplies the upper left glyph.
Upper-right glyph for this icon offset.
Lower-left glyph origin, two bytes beyond the upper-left lookup base.
Lower-right glyph origin. Each caller selects an icon through the displacement in Y.
Doubles the three-byte time count in place with decimal ADC.
Saves the original digits, doubles the counter twice and adds the saved count back in decimal mode.
Scans active actors in reverse order and tests both axes of their pose-dependent hit boxes. Returns the first overlapping slot in Y, skipping the caller’s slot and using zero for none.

Builds the player hit box from the active sprite frame and searches for overlap. Actor type $0B awards a fairy when eligible. The tenth fairy resets the counter and can add a life. Other contact follows the damage path except for type $05.
Writes A to the foreground buffer at X unless the tile probe returned $FF for an off-room sample.
Shifts stock entries toward the front, fills the tail with code $08 and redraws the stock HUD.
TIME UP! glyphs followed by zero. The timeout effect draws the string before inverting the edges around the exit.
Prints the timeout message, locates the exit tile and inverts successively larger perimeters around it. Stops when a complete perimeter has no eligible cells.
Signed horizontal step for the four edges of the timeout inversion perimeter.
Signed vertical step for the timeout perimeter edges.
Clips screen coordinates against the room and skips a central text strip. Changes the cell colors and inverts its eight bitmap bytes, then marks that a cell was reached.
Twenty-two paired row addresses for inverting cells in the playfield. The effect derives the color RAM and bitmap locations from these.
High-byte operand alias into the interleaved screen-row address table.
Lookup indexed by raw foreground tile code. Bit 0 is the solid flag used by $1C3B and $1C5E.
Maps the previous tile byte to the replacement written by a spell or an actor’s tile-changing hit. For example, $02 becomes $00 and $03 becomes $31.
Identity lookup of values $00–$3F beside the tile replacement table. The 256-byte mapping indexed through $24C0 ends at $25BF.
Maps raw, hidden or buried room cell encodings to tile-art codes when visibility conversion is enabled.
Second full-byte tile-code remap. The path at $3ADD reads it by raw tile code.
Converts each bitmap font byte before the transparent text routine overlays it using the complementary $CF00 mask.
Walks the sixteen actor slots in reverse. Active slots call one of two behavior tables selected by the phase byte at $0500 + slot.
Low operand patched from the primary actor targets.
High operand of the primary actor call, set from the corresponding high-address entry at $293B.
Low and high address halves of the actor dispatch used with a zero phase byte.
High-byte half of the primary behavior handler table, indexed by actor type.
Picks the secondary actor behavior using the type in Y and sets the JSR target from the split address table.
Low operand patched by secondary actor dispatch.
High operand of the secondary call, selected from the high-address table at $2975.
Low and high halves of the behavior targets for actor slots with a nonzero phase byte.
High-byte half of the secondary behavior table paired with lows at $2961.
Clears the active slot's phase byte, returning it to primary dispatch.
Removes the actor after a solid landing or advances its Y position and alternating temporary frame on a clear probe.
Falls through the supported-tile test, restores the saved origin and facing after writing the drop if it landed, and blanks the actor for its next cycle.
Clears the active flag for slot X.
Tests the current cell and uses the animation counter to select a replacement tile if it is empty. Requests effect $06 after restoring X.
Sixteen possible tile values for the actor drop path, selected through the threshold table at $2A1D.
Ascending bounds used to choose one of the drop tile codes from the low byte of the update counter.
Alternates its facing-dependent sprite frame and moves two units horizontally. On a solid probe, stores the struck tile and applies a three-step break animation before reversing direction.
Falls two units when the probe beneath it is non-solid, then selects a normal or countdown animation frame.

Uses its timer to animate in and out, restore its saved spawn position and facing, and run a walking phase. The walking phase falls through open floor and processes wall hits with the three-step block replacement.
Saves a home position as its appearance cycle begins, animates into view and uses facing-based frames while active. It restores home and blank frame $7F when the timer reaches the end of the cycle.
Counts down the projectile, follows tile probes and moves a signed step along its direction. An overlapping actor is sent to its secondary handler and triggers the hit sound.
Horizontal sample offsets for the projectile's candidate tile probes.
Vertical sample offsets for the matching projectile probes.
Direction codes selected by a solid result on the corresponding probe.
Four signed horizontal projectile steps indexed by direction.
Four signed vertical projectile steps indexed by direction.
Two consecutive animation frames per fireball direction.
Tests candidate probe offsets from a facing-based group. Chooses a new direction if one probe hits and moves by the corresponding signed X and Y offsets.
Candidate horizontal offsets used by the three-probe loop in the actor at $2E29.
Vertical counterparts of those three-probe offsets.
Direction selected when the probe at the corresponding candidate index finds a solid tile.
Signed X delta indexed by direction and the actor's movement selector.
Signed Y delta for the same movement index.
Alternates flying frames and moves horizontally until a solid sample. The three-stage collision animation swaps the affected tile and flips the mover's direction.
Uses the actor's state byte to patch the jump from the paired tables at $2F9D and $2FA6.
Low operand of the first floor-chaser state jump.
High operand of the first floor-chaser state jump.
Nine state-handler pointers for the actor at $2F8B. The two halves patch the operand of the dispatch JMP.
The upper address bytes corresponding to the nine targets whose low bytes are at $2F9D.
Tests for support at two offsets, then chooses falling state eight or horizontal behavior. An obstruction starts state three and records the hit tile for the tile-break path.
Decrements the hit phase, flips facing, replaces the recorded tile through the impact lookup and redraws the result.
Advances the collision state and draws tile $2F at the remembered hit cell.
Chooses a contact pose from facing and draws tile $30 at the hit cell.
Ends the first floor-chaser removal sequence by clearing its active byte.
Uses sprite frame $40 and advances this actor's disappearance state.
Uses sprite frame $3F for the next step of the first actor's disappearance.
Sets sprite color one and frame $3E before decrementing the first floor-chaser's state.
Probes the floor ahead. On contact eases the actor out of this state and starts sound $0C, otherwise adds four to its vertical coordinate and uses frame $2A plus the orientation and animation offset.
Patches the second floor-chaser jump from its state table.
Low operand of the second floor-chaser dispatch.
High operand of the second floor-chaser state jump.
Nine internal state handlers read by $3136 and copied into its jump operand.
High-byte address lane for the nine actor states dispatched at $3136.
Checks two floor samples and enters an accelerated fall if both are unsupported. Otherwise moves along the floor and selects a wall response using the sampled tile code.
Reverses the second floor-chaser after its final collision phase and substitutes the struck foreground code.
Uses the saved collision index to redraw tile $2F in the second actor's hit sequence.
Decrements the state before drawing tile $30, the other temporary impact tile.
Clears the active slot after the second floor-chaser's disappearance.
Selects $40 during the second variant's disappearance and decrements the state.
Moves the second chaser's removal timer forward with sprite frame $3F.
Sets color one and sprite $3E for the second floor-chaser, then decrements the countdown.
Probes the floor and advances the actor downward four world units on a clear sample. A solid sample advances the state and signals effect $0C.
Chooses the third variant's internal handler via $334B and $3354.
Low operand of the third floor-chaser state jump.
High operand of the third floor-chaser dispatch.
Nine internal state-handler addresses split into low and high bytes. Actor state selects one at $3339.
High-byte lane for the nine targets selected by $3339.
Checks floor support at two sample points. Enters fall state when both are open, otherwise advances left or right or begins the wall-hit states.
Decrements the hit countdown, reverses the third variant and applies the recorded tile's replacement.
Draws the $2F impact tile, using the third variant's saved cell after decrementing its state.
Advances the third actor's hit phase and draws the second temporary tile value $30.
Clears the active slot for the third floor-chaser.
Selects pointer $40 and advances the third variant's removal state.
Updates the third actor's removal frame to $3F and decrements the state byte.
Writes color one and first removal frame $3E for the third actor, then updates state.
On a clear floor sample increments Y four times. A blocked sample decrements the state and starts sound $0C.

Moves diagonally in one of four directions when the two relevant probes are clear. On a hit picks a new direction using the raster value and frame counter. A separate timer selects its disappearance frames.
The first lookup at this address aliases the return opcode; the disappearance state uses nonzero indices into the following frame bytes.
Disappearance frame indices followed by the four frame bases used for the diagonal movement directions.
Starting sprite frame for each direction of the diagonal mover.
One of the actor-table entries that return without changing the actor slot.
Separate return target in the actor dispatch table, immediately before the vertical mover.
Moves up or down until the tile probe hits a solid cell. Stores the cell and replaces it through a three-phase tile animation, then reverses its vertical direction.
High byte of the jump to the tile-blit path at the end of the vertical mover.
Chooses a frame and tile sample from the current heading. Steps when clear and uses a timed hit progression to redraw a solid cell.
Pairs of sprite frames for each heading used by the four-direction tile breaker.
Counts down to phase two, then looks for a free actor slot and creates a type $10 projectile at the emitter with the inherited facing and a sound effect.
Fills a free actor slot with type $10, the emitter's position and its associated direction and sprite shape, then starts effect zero.
Decrements the slot's animation counter. Selects a frame from $3A–$3D, or changes the actor type to $13 when the countdown ends.
Empty actor-table target preceding the player dispatcher.
Checks overlaps, then dispatches the player’s state from $0440 through the address assembled in $02/$03.
Eight player handlers split into high and low halves. Includes upright, crouching, airborne, dying and both casting phases.
Eight high bytes of the player-state targets. The dispatch at $36DC selects the pair by $0440.
Sets state zero and the standing sprite frame selected by facing, unless the player is already in state zero.
Sets state one and the crouched sprite frame for the direction the player faces.

Eight bitmap bytes per glyph. The text blitters multiply a glyph code by eight, add $FC00 and copy or mask the resulting rows. Usable glyphs appear at the ASCII positions for letters and digits, with game icons in additional slots.
